title: SAML HTTP-Artifact Binding
subtitle: SP-initiated SSO where the browser only ever carries a small artifact reference — the SP fetches the real assertion over a back-channel SOAP call the Network tab never sees.

steps.label: Open a protected SP page
steps.lede: The user navigates to a protected resource. As with any SP-initiated flow the SP needs a fresh assertion — but here it will collect it by reference, not by value.
steps.devtools: Open DevTools (F12) → Network, enable Preserve log and Disable cache. The key thing you will not see later is the assertion itself — only a short SAMLart.

steps.label: SP redirects with an AuthnRequest
steps.lede: No local session, so the SP builds an AuthnRequest asking the IdP to reply over the HTTP-Artifact binding, and redirects the browser with the DEFLATE+base64 SAMLRequest.
steps.code:
URL-decode → base64-decode → INFLATE (raw DEFLATE)

<samlp:AuthnRequest
    ID="_synthetic-req-0000000000000000000000001"
    Version="2.0"
    IssueInstant="2026-07-25T15:04:05Z"
    Destination="https://idp.example.net/sso/redirect"
    ProtocolBinding="urn:oasis:names:tc:SAML:2.0:bindings:HTTP-Artifact"
    AssertionConsumerServiceURL="https://sp.example.com/saml/acs">
  <saml:Issuer>https://sp.example.com/saml/metadata</saml:Issuer>
</samlp:AuthnRequest>
steps.devtools: Find the 302 to the IdP. URL-decode → base64-decode → INFLATE the SAMLRequest; note ProtocolBinding = …:HTTP-Artifact — that is what makes the IdP reply with a reference instead of the assertion.

steps.label: IdP authenticates and mints an artifact
steps.lede: The IdP authenticates the user (or reuses an existing session), builds the Response + signed Assertion, stores it, and mints a one-time artifact (SourceID + MessageHandle) to hand back.
steps.devtools: The IdP may show its login page first (absent under a live session). The important response is the 302 back to the SP ACS — its Location carries a SAMLart, not a SAMLResponse.

steps.label: ACS receives only the artifact
steps.lede: The browser is redirected to the ACS carrying just the 44-byte artifact reference in SAMLart, alongside RelayState. The assertion itself never transits the front channel.
steps.devtools: Select the GET to /saml/acs → Query String Parameters. You will see an opaque SAMLart and RelayState — and crucially no SAMLResponse and no assertion. This is the whole point of the artifact binding.

steps.label: Back-channel ArtifactResolve (SOAP)
steps.lede: The SP dereferences the artifact over a signed SOAP ArtifactResolve to the IdP's Artifact Resolution Service, on a mutually authenticated TLS channel. This call is server-to-server.
steps.codeTitle: Signed SOAP ArtifactResolve (not in the browser)
steps.devtools: Not visible in DevTools. This SOAP POST goes SP → IdP directly, so capture it with server logs or an mTLS-aware proxy, not the browser Network tab. The ARS checks the artifact was issued for this calling SP.

steps.label: Back-channel ArtifactResponse (SOAP)
steps.lede: The ARS finds the artifact, deletes it (one-time use), and returns an ArtifactResponse wrapping the original Response + signed Assertion. The SP now validates it exactly as in POST-binding SSO.

jwt.title: Decoded SAML Assertion (XML)
payload: IdP entityID — validate against IdP metadata before trusting anything
The ACS URL this Response is bound to
Must equal the AuthnRequest ID from step 2
Gates acceptance; Responder / AuthnFailed mean reject
Validity bounds — allow small clock skew
Ties to the SSO session — needed later for Single Logout

steps.devtools: Not visible in DevTools. A valid, unused artifact yields the assertion; an expired or already-dereferenced artifact returns an empty ArtifactResponse by design, so a caller learns nothing about a handle it should not hold. Verify the Signature before reading claims.

steps.label: SP session created, land on RelayState
steps.lede: With the resolved assertion validated, the SP creates its session, sets a cookie, and redirects the browser to the RelayState target.

headers: assertion resolved via back-channel SOAP ArtifactResolve, not shown in browser

steps.devtools: Back in the browser: the ACS answers 302 to the RelayState deep link and sets sp_session. The assertion that authorised this never appeared on the wire you can see.

steps.label: Signed in
steps.lede: The browser follows the redirect with the new cookie and the protected page renders. The artifact is already consumed and cannot be resolved again.
steps.devtools: Nothing further on the wire. Because the browser only ever held a reference, a stolen SAMLart URL is useless once the SP has resolved it — the ARS returns empty on any replay.
